chapter: Freelancing, Miller and the girls' bands
title: Touring with Ina Ray Hutton's all-woman band
summary: He traveled with Hutton's band for a year, hand-picked musicians, imported a British first trumpeter, and wrote for a ten-week Chicago broadcast.

bands.name: Ina Ray Hutton and Her Orchestra

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, what sort of work do you do now? All kinds, I take it, not just instrumentals, but sort of song arrangements?
I haven't been doing any outside arranging. I just wrote up a lot of charts for myself.
No, I mean this period when you're with --
Basie?
No, after Basie, when you're arranging for Glenn Miller, Artie Shaw, Ina Ray, what did you do?
Well, I traveled with Ina for a year. I traveled with the band all over the country.
Oh, you did?
Yeah, I traveled with that band.
How good a band was that?

It got to be a very good band. But the musicians, you had to hand pick them. I had to send to London, England to get a first trumpet player, because there wasn't a woman here that could reach even a high C. But I didn't use many high C's, but they couldn't even reach a good F with volume, so they sent me a girl from out of England, from the Conservatory and she could reach that note, so that band was pretty rough.
Because --
Did she have the usual instrumentation?
We used four saxes, and -- five, let me say. Yeah, four trumpets, three trombones and five saxes. That's what we had.
Did Ina sing?
Yeah.
And conduct.
Yeah, and could sing. Her clarinet playing wasn't fast enough. They all quit playing when I started writing for the band. The leaders wouldn't play no more. They were afraid of the arrangements.
And you travelled with them, too. Did you rehearse them, I suppose?

Oh, yeah, I'd rehearse them. Most times I picked the openings, just like one of the managers with the Giants. He pick who he want to open, I'd pick songs according to the audience in the theaters and places, because Ina couldn't do that.
Well, how popular was that band then?

Very, very popular. They had a -- we went ten weeks coast to coast in Chicago, the Choice Hour. Bing Crosby had it on one station at 10:00 and she had it on the hour, that way. And that was her only competition. That was the Rose Bowl, ten weeks. And I went out there three or four weeks ahead of time, and -- maybe Earl might remember this. I went out there three or four weeks ahead of time to

to write the show, write music strictly for that broadcast. They had a big broadcast. And Earl was there, and he sent his car up and his chauffeur while he was gone, three or four weeks. And I had his car, whatever his car was. He probably forgot. And he'd say, use my car while you're gone.
Somebody run into it and hit it with a while I had it.
